key_insight: A localized hybrid FEM–random feature method solves interface problems by using standard finite elements away from the interface and random-feature models only in cut-cell bands near the interface.
engineering_relevance: This reduces global surrogate complexity while handling high-contrast jumps and irregular interface geometries on unfitted meshes, making it attractive for multiphysics and heterogeneous-material simulations.
method: Use Qp finite elements on uncut background cells.
Use local random-feature representations only in interface-cut cells on both physical sides of Γ.
Enforce solution/flux jumps on Γ and couple FEM–RFM across an artificial grid-aligned interface Γc via trace and flux residuals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests in 2D and 3D on high-contrast, nonsmooth, multiple-interface, and irregular-boundary cases, plus a thermal-homogenization application for a periodic bicontinuous composite.
watch_item: The method depends on accurate cut-cell identification and stable coupling/residual minimization, which may be sensitive in very thin interface bands or highly complex geometries.
paper_title: A Localized Hybrid Finite Element--Random Feature Method for Elliptic Interface Problems on Unfitted Meshes
